data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services is often *less* resilient to correlated failure than one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy, due to premature exhaustion of recovery resources under cascading loads.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the large service's internal redundancy is concentrated in a monoculture, then the decentralized network is more resilient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there is a central, well-provisioned load-shedding circuit breaker governing the decentralized network's routing layer.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shocks are truly independent (not common-cause traffic shocks).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independently operated small services often lack backstop resources. A common-cause shock (e.g., a traffic spike or cache stampede) that a large service's redundant pools absorb can trigger simultaneous outages across many small services, meaning the observed joint failure distribution is dominated by correlated causes hidden as independent failures.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
